title: Pre-Analysis — Extension of the Flame Penetration Resistant Lining Standard
abstract: Closed pre-analysis of a proposed revision extending the flame penetration resistant lining laminate from the forward and aft compartments to the bulk compartment sidewall and to the aft compartment ceiling void.

sections.objective: Assess whether the laminate standard introduced for the cargo compartment lining panels can be extended to the bulk compartment sidewall and the aft compartment ceiling void without a new qualification, and establish what the extension would do to the retrofit bulletin, the parts list and the wiring that is clipped to the panel back faces. The request came from a fleet campaign review that found the two remaining areas were the only ones still lined to the original standard.
sections.findings_summary: The extension was not supported as scoped. The bulk compartment sidewall is already the subject of a separate candidate that proposes a thermal barrier quilt over the same wall for live animal transport, and neither document cites the other because the two are written in entirely different vocabulary; laminating the wall and quilting it are mutually exclusive as currently drawn. The retrofit bulletin's kit list is built around the panel sizes of the two compartments it covers and would have to be reissued rather than amended. The compartment lighting and smoke detection wiring is clipped to the back face of the panels in the ceiling void, and the laminate's greater thickness moves every clip position. The parts list impact is straightforward and follows whichever scope is agreed.
sections.next_steps: The work order was closed with the extension returned for rescoping. The bulk compartment sidewall is to be settled first between the two design offices, since one wall cannot take both treatments; the recommendation is that the aft compartment ceiling void is separated out and progressed on its own, where the only real obstacle is the wiring clip survey. The bulletin owner was asked not to amend the kit list until the scope is fixed.

similarity_seeds: cargo compartment wall lining and liner burn through resistance

tasks.title: Search all cargo compartment wall and ceiling treatments in work
Survey the wiring clip positions on the panel back faces
Check the retrofit bulletin kit list against the proposed areas

evidence.similarity_note: Two proposals for the same physical wall, retrieved only by similarity. One speaks of a flame penetration resistant laminate on a cargo lining panel, the other of a thermal barrier quilt for live animal transport. They share no part number, no FIN, no zone and no ATA chapter, and neither cites the other.

expected_findings.rationale: The bulk compartment sidewall cannot carry both a bonded laminate panel and a quilted barrier: the quilt needs the standoff the laminate thickness consumes, and the two attachment schemes use the same stud rows. As drawn, whichever is embodied first excludes the other.
expected_findings.resolution: Settle the wall between the two design offices before either scope is fixed. Recommendation is to hold the laminate extension on the bulk sidewall and progress the aft ceiling void separately.

expected_findings.rationale: The bulletin's kit list is built around the panel sizes of the two compartments it covers and its accomplishment time is quoted per compartment. Adding two areas with different panel geometry would leave the kit list incomplete on its own effectivity, which is a reissue rather than an amendment.
expected_findings.resolution: Hold the bulletin unchanged until the scope is fixed, then reissue it with one kit per compartment rather than one kit per aircraft.

expected_findings.rationale: The compartment lighting and smoke detection harnesses are clipped to the back face of the lining panels in the ceiling void. The laminate is thicker than the panel it replaces and every clip position moves, which the sheet shows to the millimetre in the forward compartment and not at all in the two proposed areas.
expected_findings.resolution: Complete the clip survey for the aft ceiling void before the scope is refixed, and update the sheet with the laminate standoff.

expected_findings.rationale: The figure would gain the two additional panel families and the longer studs that go with the laminate thickness. The impact is real but entirely mechanical and follows whichever scope is finally agreed.
expected_findings.resolution: No action from this work order; the figure change is to be raised with the rescoped modification.

expected_non_findings.reason: Shares the forward compartment zones and reads as a cargo compartment document, so it ranks in the first page of both passes. It isolates a smoke warning with no smoke found and its reasoning is about airflow through the sampling line, which no lining material changes.

type_data.conclusion: Issued 2026-07-02. The extension was rejected as scoped on the bulk sidewall overlap; the aft ceiling void is viable once the wiring clip survey is complete.
